Windows, and there are no screenshots. Details: `docs/scene_right_click_add.md`.

## 7u. Physics: crates that stand, a playground, materials, a slider and debris

**What it is.** The physics got a second way to solve contacts, called **Improved** (the old one is **Classic**; old scenes keep it, new scenes
get Improved). Crates stack and stay put, a ball bounces and rolls to a stop, fast bullets stop at thin walls, resting things go to sleep
(cheap) and wake when what holds them up goes away. Also new: a physics material on every collider (icy or bouncy floors), a **Slider** joint, ropes that
stay near their length, joints in the physics debug view and a debris emitter. Plain explanation and the numbers: [physics.md](physics.md) and
[physics_plan.md](physics_plan.md). Code: `Physics/Physics3DImproved.inl`, `Physics/ContactSolver.hpp`, `Physics/BoxManifold.hpp`,
`Physics/DebrisPool.hpp`.

**How to reach it.**

1. Open the editor (`Tools\OkayEngine.exe`, or the launcher). Use **File > Open Scene** and pick `examples\physics\physics_playground.okayscene`
   (it ships next to the editor in the zip and the installer). The scene looks like a big grey floor with nine small stations.
2. Press **Play**. Everything starts at once. Wait about 10 seconds.
3. To compare with the old physics: stop Play, open **Project Settings > Physics**, under "Physics quality of the open scene" choose
   **Classic**, press Play again. Change it back to **Improved**. (The choice is saved with the scene.)

**What you should see (Improved).**

| Station | What to look for |
|---|---|
| 1 Tower | Five crates stand in a column, hardly move, and (after about a second) go to sleep. In Classic the tower leans and falls. |
| 2 Ball | A red ball rolls down a short ramp, bounces and rolls to a slow stop on the floor. |
| 3 Ramps | Three ramps at 20 degrees, the same green crate on each: the plain and the rubber ramp hold it, the icy (light blue) one lets it slide off. The ramps' friction is set per collider (Physics Material). |
| 4 Bullet | A small red ball fires at 60 m/s at a 5 cm thin wall and stops at it. In Classic it goes through. |
| 5 Heavy and light | A 100 kg steel crate is pushed at 5 m/s and shoves the 1 kg wooden crate ahead of it. |
| 6 Pads | The same blue ball dropped on a dark pad (dead) and a black rubber pad (bounces many times; the pad's own bounciness 0.92). |
| 7 Rope | Six balls on distance joints swing from a hook and hang about 5 m long, close to their real length. |
| 8 Slider | A blue drawer slides 3 m along x at 1 m/s and stops at its limit. |
| 9 Debris | A burst of small brown chunks every 1.5 seconds: they fly, land, go to sleep, shrink away. There are never more than 150. |

To see the joints and sleeping bodies: **View > Scene Overlays > Physics Debug > Show physics (Scene + Game)**. Colliders are green, sleeping
ones grey, contacts red, joints orange.

**Try the new settings yourself.**

* Select the **3 Ramp ice** object, find its collider in the Inspector, open **Physics Material**, tick **Own Friction** and set it to 2: the crate now holds.
* Select any crate, **Rigidbody 3D**: **Rolling Resistance** (0 = a ball rolls on for ever, 0.03 default). **Use Child Colliders** makes colliders on child objects part of the body.
* Select the **8 Drawer**, **Joint 3D** (mode **Slider**): change **Max Travel** or **Motor Speed**.
* Select **9 Debris emitter**: **Count**, **Interval**, **Max Active**, **Settled Life**.
* Add your own: **Add Component > Physics 3D > DebrisEmitter** on an empty object, then Play. In code, `DebrisPool` spawns chunks at your own moments (a digger, an explosion).

**Screenshots (headless Linux software renders of the same scene, not the editor window; camera and look differ from the editor):**


**Status.** Tested headless on Linux (`tests/test_physics_deep_*.cpp`: manifold, solver, bugs, improved, save, more; the existing physics, joint, hinge,
ragdoll, vehicle, destructible, controller and net-prediction tests stay green). The playground was played headless for 10 seconds and the
positions listed in the plan were read back. **Unverified:** the editor menus and Inspector rows on Windows (they were compiled, not opened), how the scene looks and feels in the real
editor or player, any real GPU. The 2D step has no Improved solver yet (the setting is saved but 2D plays as before).

## 7v. Test builds: try a branch before it is released

**What it is.** Today a change waits about an hour for the pull-request checks, is merged, and then a release builds for 15 to 30 minutes before you
can see it. A **test build** skips all of that: the coordinator builds one branch for you, it is published to its own folder on the update server,
and your launcher offers it **only if you switched "Get test builds" on**. It never touches the normal "latest" update, and a normal player never
sees it. It may be broken: that is what a test is. Rules and files: [release_channels.md](release_channels.md#test-builds-for-the-owner-to-try-a-branch-not-a-channel-for-players).

**How to try it.**

1. **Ask the coordinator** to start a test build of a branch ("start a test build of walk-vs-run"). They start the workflow **Test build (dev
   channel)** from `main`; it takes **about 15 to 30 minutes**. When it is done its page says "Test build published", the version (for example
   `2.876.0.17`) and the branch. You cannot start it yourself: it needs GitHub, and it only runs from `main`.
2. In the launcher open **Settings** (the sidebar), the **Behavior** tab, the card **STARTUP & UPDATES**, and switch **Get test builds** on. A
   message says "Test builds are on. They can be broken. Switch this off here to stop getting them."
3. **What you should see** within a minute or so (or click the version number at the top of the sidebar to look right now):
   * a message "Test build of walk-vs-run (abc1234) is ready (v2.876.0.17)";
   * in the sidebar a card **Test build available** with the text "Test build of walk-vs-run (abc1234) is ready" and an **Install now** button.
4. Press **Install now**. The **Software Update** window shows `v2.876.0 » v2.876.0.17`, the line **Test build of walk-vs-run (abc1234)** in amber,
   and the coordinator's note under "What's new". It downloads and checks the files like any update (a file that does not match its checksum is
   refused and nothing is installed). When it says "Update installed" press **Restart now**.
5. After the restart: **Settings > About** says "Version 2.876.0.17 (test build)" and, under it in amber, "Test build of walk-vs-run (abc1234)";
   the sidebar version says `v2.876.0.17 test`; the editor's **Help > About** says `v2.876.0.17 (test build)` and its window title ends in
   `[v2.876.0.17 (test build)]`; the **Versions** page says "You're running v2.876.0.17 (test build)".
6. **To stop getting test builds:** Settings > Behavior > Startup & updates > switch **Get test builds** off. A message says "Test builds are off.
   Nothing new will be offered." (**Reset preferences** on the same tab also turns it off.)
7. **To go back to the stable version** (while a test build is installed): close the editor, then in the same card press **Go back to the stable
   version** (it shows when Get test builds is off; the row above it names the test build you run). The update window says "Going back to the
   newest normal release (a test build is replaced)" and `v2.876.0.17 » v2.876.0`; press **Restart now**. After the restart About says "Version
   2.876.0" with no test line. (Otherwise the next normal release replaces the test build by itself.)
8. If the launcher does not start at all after a test build: run `OkaySpace-Setup.exe` from the normal release page over the top; it is a normal
   installer and replaces everything.

**Limits.** A test build replaces only the launcher, the editor and the player, like any in-app update. If a branch adds an example scene or another
file that ships in the zip or installer (the `examples\` folder), that file is **not** in the test build: ask for it separately or wait for a release.

**How to tell it is on or off.** With the switch off the launcher never asks the update server for the test folder, so nothing about test builds
can appear. With it on, the launcher reads `dev/versions.json` on the update server; the file `dev/DEV.txt` there names the newest test build.

**Status.** Checked on Linux, not on Windows:
`dev_channel` (16,516 checks: the version order, the normal reader ignoring test versions, the test reader, the signature rule, the setting, the
same install rules), `self_update` (the way back is judged strictly), `dev_publish_script` (the publisher against a fake storage server: only `dev/`
is written, in order, the real release files are byte for byte unchanged, and every refusal writes nothing), `dev_index` (self-test) and
`dev_workflow_lint` (the workflow read and its shell steps run offline). The launcher and editor files were compiled with `g++ -fsyntax-only` and
the MinGW win32 compiler; they were not built or run. **Never run:** the workflow on GitHub, a write to the real Supabase storage, anything on Windows,
and every screen above (no screenshot: the launcher was not built here). The wording in step 3 to 7 is what the code says; tell us what you actually see.

## 7w. Player obstacle course and the player's own numbers

Where: `examples\player\player_obstacle_course.okayscene` (next to the other examples, see "Where the files are"). Open it in
`Tools\OkayEngine.exe` with **File > Open...** and press **Play**, or open it in `Tools\OkaySpacePlayer.exe`. You start on the ground
with a third-person player. **WASD** walk, **Shift** run, **Space** jump, **Ctrl** crouch, **V** switches to the eyes and back.
**Press F3**: below the frame numbers you see the player's lines (grounded or in the air, slope in degrees against the limit,
speed, velocity, the ground normal, what you stand on). In the editor the same lines are in the Game view stats.

Walk -Z (straight ahead) past the signs. Each sign says what to try; what you should see:

| Station | Try | You should see |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Ramps 15, 30, 45, 55, 65 degrees | walk up each, stop half way up | 15 to 45: you walk up and stand still on it with no creeping (F3: "held on slope"). 55 and 65: you slide back down; F3 says TOO STEEP |
| 2 Stairs | walk up, turn, walk down | you stay on the steps going down (F3 stays "grounded"), no hopping |
| 3 Steps 0.10, 0.25, 0.35, 0.60 m | walk into each | the first three you climb in one go, the 0.60 m block stops you |
| 4 Plank over a gap | walk along it, step off the side | you fall into the gap, nothing sticks |
| 5 Tunnel 1.3 m | crouch (Ctrl), go in, press Ctrl again inside | you fit when crouched; standing up inside is refused until you are out |
| 6 Moving platform and turning bridge | stand on the platform, jump off sideways | you ride it with no slipping; jumping off keeps the platform's speed; the bridge carries you round |
| 7 Thin wall (2 cm) | hold Shift and run into it | you stop; you do not get through |
| 8 Water | walk into the shallow end, then the deep end | shallow: you wade; deep: you swim (Space up, Ctrl down). (Swim into the stone edge on the east side to climb out.) |
| 9 Voxel terrain patch | walk over the hill and the hole | you follow the ground without bouncing |
| 10 Ladder tower | walk into the ladder and hold W; let go; press Space | you climb at 2.5 m/s, hang still when you let go, Space jumps off; the jump down from the top is a "hard landing" (F3 shows "last landing ... hard landings N") |
| 11 Pool bank (east edge of the pool) | swim to the stone edge and keep pushing W | you climb out onto the bank (before, you stayed in the water) |
| Variable jump (the course player has it on) | tap Space, then hold Space | a tap is a short hop, holding is the full jump. Off in a fresh player (Inspector: Variable Jump) |
| Gizmo | in the editor select the player | a blue ring at the feet, four orange spokes rising at the Slope Limit, a green ring at the Step Offset height (Scene view, Gizmos on) |

**Compare with the old player**: close the game, set the environment variable `OKAY_OLD_PLAYER=1` (for example in a command
prompt: `set OKAY_OLD_PLAYER=1` then start `OkaySpacePlayer.exe` from that prompt, or start the editor from it), and walk the same
stations. F3 then adds "[old player path]" to the first player line. With it set: standing on ramps 25 to 49 degrees creeps, the
stairs down hop, a jump from the platform loses its speed, and every frame costs more (see `docs/player_audit.md`).

Settings you can now change and that are saved: select the player, the **Player Controller** panel, **Step Offset** and **Slope
Limit** (first and third person).

**Pictures** (headless software render, flat shading, no signs or water shine, made by `tests/render_course.cpp`): a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) (`02_ramps.png`, `07_f3_player_lines_on_30_degree_ramp.png` shows the F3 lines as the 8x8 font draws them; the real F3 panel was not seen).

**Checks run here (Linux, headless)**: `tests/test_player_deep.cpp` (860 checks, each fails with `OKAY_OLD_PLAYER=1`),
`tests/test_player_course.cpp` (the shipped file is what the code writes, and a player walks stations 1, 3, 7), and the older player,
controller, stance, character and multiplayer prediction tests: all pass. Frame numbers: `docs/player_audit.md`.
**Not seen:** Windows, a window, a picture of the course (none was made), the F3 text on screen, the Inspector fields, real feel.

## 7wa. Player feel lab: compare five controller feels, and see which system costs the frame

Where: `examples\player\player_feel_lab.okayscene`. Open it in `Tools\OkayEngine.exe` (**File > Open...**, **Play**) or in
`Tools\OkaySpacePlayer.exe`. You start in third person at the start sign. **WASD** walk, **Shift** run, **Space** jump, **Ctrl** crouch,
**V** switches to the eyes and back.

**Switch the feel.** Press **1 Classic, 2 Modern, 3 Arcade, 4 Realistic, 5 Shooter**. The sign at the start changes to
"PRESET: <name>", and **F3** shows "feel preset: <name>" under the player lines. Walk the stations after each pick:

| Station | Try | You should see (numbers are from the headless tests, `tests/test_player_feel.cpp`) |
|---|---|---|
| A Run track, markers every 5 m | hold W + Shift, let go at the red line | Arcade stops in about 0.14 m, Classic 0.27 m, Realistic 0.50 m (it also takes longer to get going) |
| B Slalom | weave through the posts | Arcade and Shooter turn sharply; Realistic turns slowly (third person turn speed) |
| C Gaps 2, 3, 4 m | run and jump | Arcade has a double jump, Realistic has the least air steering (about 1.0 m/s sideways against 2.6 for Arcade). A miss drops into the pit and returns you to the start |
| D Towers 2, 4, 8 m | climb the stairs, step off | the camera dips on landing (Realistic most, Arcade least); the 8 m drop is a hard landing (F3 counts them) |
| E Corridor | walk through in third person | the camera pulls in at the walls and eases back out |

**In your own scene.** Select the player, the **Player Controller** panel, **Controller Preset** drop-down: one pick sets speeds,
acceleration, stopping, air control, jump timing, head bob (first person) or turn speed and camera follow (third person). Edit any
value afterwards; the scene saves the numbers. The same panel has **Stick Look Ramp** (gamepad camera acceleration: seconds from 45%
to full look speed at full stick; 0 = off, the default) and, on **Player View**, **Preset Hotkeys (1-5)** (off by default; the lab
has it on; it needs the player to have both views).

**Systems page (F3, second press).** In `OkaySpacePlayer.exe` press F3 once for the frame numbers, again for **Systems**:
milliseconds per system (Physics, Scripts, Animation, Audio, UI, Render, Terrain, Other CPU, Idle/wait) averaged over the last 120
frames with their peaks, and a graph of the last 120 frame times. A third press closes it. In the editor, **Game view > Stats overlay**
shows the same rows while playing (Audio and Render rows are filled by the player only; the editor shows UI and the scene's own
scopes). It measures only while the page is open.

**Compare with before.** `set OKAY_OLD_PLAYER=1` brings back the old player behaviour. `set OKAY_OLD_SCENE_QUERIES=1` brings back
the old scene-wide searches (see the numbers below).

**Checks run here (Linux, headless):** `tests/test_player_feel.cpp` (127 checks: presets, saved, hotkeys, stick ramp, camera
steadiness at 30/60/144/240 fps, eye bob range, foot sliding of the real controller for all presets walking and running, system
rows), `tests/test_player_feel_lab.cpp` (the shipped scene is what the code writes; 1-5 switch the preset), and the player,
controller, net prediction, character and locomotion tests. Frame numbers of the busy scene: `docs/player_audit.md` (section
"Busy scene").
**Not seen:** Windows, a window, the Inspector drop-down, the F3 systems page on a screen, the lab scene on a screen, gamepad
feel with a real pad, whether the preset numbers feel right (they were chosen by measurement and by reasoning, not by playing).

## 7z. First-person arm: normal for you and for everyone else

**What it is.** Your own arm in first person (the player in the First Person starter). Before: no arm unless you held
something, then a floating skin block, and a left click did nothing. Now: a hand and forearm in your shirt colour, always in
view at the lower right, a left click swings it, and other players see the whole body. Before and after pictures:
a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) and a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) (headless renders: left your camera, middle a camera in
front of the player, right a camera at the side). Details: [fp_hand.md](fp_hand.md).

**How to try it (Windows release).**

1. Open the editor, open `examples\fp_hand\fp_hand_test.okayscene` (the `examples` folder next to the program) and press Play.
2. Look at the lower right of your view: you should see a hand with a forearm in a green sleeve coming up from the bottom edge. Click
   the left mouse button: the arm swings.
3. Walk up to a block (red cube, blue block, green box), press **E** to hold it. It sits in the hand. The green box is two-handed.
4. The small picture at the top right is a second camera looking back at you: you should see a whole person with two arms, the
   held block in the hand and the arm swinging when you click. No floating hand there.
5. Stop. Select **Player**, in the Inspector find **First Person Hands**, open **Preset** and pick Both arms (looks like Normal except for two-handed items, see fp_hand.md), Right hand
   only, Minimal (just the hand block) or **Old look**; press Play each time. **Use normal first-person arms** brings the normal look back (Ctrl+Z also undoes it).
   **Open Preview** shows both views live as you change a preset.

**Unverified.** Everything above is checked only by the tests (`ctest -R fp_hand`) and headless software renders on Linux.
The editor window code compiles but was not run; no Windows, GPU, or real multiplayer session was tried; how it feels in a real game is unknown.

## 7zg. Guided modeling: a fence from designs, then your own edits

**What it is.** The existing Modeling window has a new **Guided** page. You pick a category, a thing (today only the
**Fence**), a starting design, and get a normal editable mesh. You can change its settings, swap parts, and keep
modeling by hand; rebuilding never overwrites your hand edits without asking. Written from general parametric
modeling; no code, models or assets from other projects. Design: `docs/guided_modeling_design.md`.

**Status.** The generation, the rebuild rules, the files and undo are tested on Linux (`ctest -R guided_modeling`, about
600 checks). The editor page (`editor/GuidedPanel.cpp`) compiles but nobody has opened it in a real window yet, and
nothing here ran on Windows. Pictures in a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) are headless software renders of the generated
meshes (our own small rasteriser), not screenshots of the editor.

**Try it (the example scene).**

1. Open `Tools\OkayEngine.exe`, **File > Open...**, paste the path to `examples\modeling\guided_fences.okayscene`
   (next to `OkaySpace.exe`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OkaySpace\examples\modeling\` for the installer). You should see eight
   fences in a row: picket, post and rail, ranch, wrought iron, chain link, stockade, low decorative, picket with a gate.
2. Click one fence in the Hierarchy. Open **View > Editors & Tools > Modeling** and press **Guided** (first in the list).
   You should see "Customise: Fence ..." with sliders.
3. Drag **Height** and let go. The fence rebuilds and the console says "Updated ...".
4. Under **Parts and materials** change **Pickets and bars** to another design, or the **Posts** design. Change a colour.
5. Open **Each part**, a kind (for example Pickets), press **Select** on one part: it jumps into Edit Mesh with that part's
   faces selected. Move it (G), then go back to the Guided page. Its row now says "[edited by you]".
6. Drag **Height** again. A window asks what to do with the part you edited: **Keep my edits**, **Discard my edits** or
   **Convert to regular mesh**. Try Keep: that part stays as you left it, everything else follows the new height.
   Pressing Cancel changes nothing.
7. In Edit Mesh add something of your own (Add page: a Cube, or extrude a face). Change a setting on the Guided page: your
   addition stays exactly where it was. This is the "your own faces are never touched" rule.
8. **Detach** on a part row, or **Convert to regular mesh**, are explicit: the part (or the whole model) stops following the
   design and stays as plain mesh. **Undo guided step** steps back.

**Try it (make a new one).** Modeling > Guided with nothing selected (or press "Make another one"): press a category
(Vehicles, Characters, Environment, Props say "No designs here yet", on purpose), pick **Fence**, click a starting design
card (pictures are drawn by our own renderer), give it a name and press **Create**. A mesh asset `Assets/<Name>.okaymesh` and
`Assets/<Name>.okayguided` appear in the Project panel.

**Your own parts and templates.** Select faces in Edit Mesh, then Guided > **My parts and templates**: type a name, pick
which kind of part it fits, **Save selection as part**. It then appears in that kind's design list (and in "Each part"). **Save
as template** keeps the whole setup; it shows as another card next to the built-in designs. Files are in
`Assets/GuidedTemplates/` (`.okaypart`, `.okaytemplate`, plain text); copy them to another project to reuse them.

**Not done or not verified (said plainly).** Only the fence exists; walls, stairs, doors, windows, roofs, vehicles,
characters, environment and props come in a later phase. The path is a list of typed points (no drawing in the 3D view). No
collider is added. Material numbers are stored but only colours are drawn today (per-face materials are a separate open
item). The Guided page's look and feel in a real window is unverified.

## 7zh. Modeling: material slots and Repair Mesh

**What it is.** The 3D modeler can now give faces to numbered material slots. Each slot has a colour, and changing a slot's colour
recolours every face in it at once. Slots are saved in the scene and in `.okaymesh` files. There is also a **Repair Mesh** button
that cleans up a broken or imported mesh in one click. Slots are colours only for now: per-slot pictures (textures) and shaders are
not built.

**Try the example.**
1. Open `Tools\OkayEngine.exe`, then **File > Open...** and pick `examples\modeling_tools\material_slots.okayscene`.
2. You should see two objects: **Slot House** (cream walls, a red roof, a brown floor and a blue door) and **Slot Ball** (a white
   ball with a green top and an orange bottom). Nothing else is needed: the colours come from the slots.
3. Click **Slot House**, open the **Modeling** window (the menu bar), tick **Edit Mesh**, open the **Paint** area and find **Material Slots**.
   You should see four rows: Slot 0 to Slot 3, each with a round button, a face count and a colour box.
4. Click the colour box of **Slot 1** and pick green. Both roof faces turn green at once. Press **Ctrl+Z**: the roof is red again.
5. Press key **3** (face mode), click one wall. Click the round button of **Slot 3**, press **Assign Sel**. That wall takes the door colour.
   Press **Select Slot** with Slot 3 chosen: the door and that wall are selected. **Clear Slots** removes all slots and the colours they gave (the mesh goes back to its plain colour).
6. Save the scene (Ctrl+S), close it and open it again: the slots and colours are still there.

**Try Repair Mesh.** Select any object with a mesh, tick **Edit Mesh**, press **Delete Faces** on a face or two to make a hole, then
**Repair Mesh**. The hole is capped and the Console says what was done, for example `Repair Mesh: merged 0 verts, capped 1 holes, flipped 0 faces; open edges 4 -> 0 (closed)`.

**Files.** `examples\modeling_tools\slot_house.okaymesh` and `slot_ball.okaymesh` are the same two models as plain files: in the Inspector set **Mesh File**
to one of them (it is in the Modeling window; the exact tab is unverified), or open one in a text editor to see the `slot N r g b a` lines.


**More modeling tools (same example folder).** Open `examples\modeling_tools\spin_path_curve.okayscene`. You should see a blue **Spun Vase**, a **Bent Horn**
(a box with a curved horn pulled out of its top) and a row of small cubes called **Curve Array** following a curve. a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) is a
headless software render of it.
1. **Array Along Curve.** Click **Curve Array**. In the Inspector find **Modifiers**: the first one is *Array Along Curve*, with a time like `0.05 ms` under its name.
   Drag one of the curve points: the cubes follow. Press **Wave** or **Helix** or **Arc**: the row takes that shape. Untick **Follow the curve**: the cubes stop turning.
   Open its **...** menu and press **Copy**: a second identical modifier appears below it (the row is now doubled); **Remove** it again.
2. **Spin.** Click **Spun Vase**, open the Modeling window, tick **Edit Mesh**, press key **2** (edge mode) and click one edge of the vase, then press **Spin**
   (Y axis, 360 deg, 16 steps): a ring of new faces is made around the vase. Ctrl+Z removes it.
3. **Extrude Along Path.** Click **Bent Horn** (or a cube), Edit Mesh, key **3** (faces), click the top face, choose **Arc**, press **Extrude Along Path**: a bent arm grows out of the face.
4. **Measuring.** In Edit Mesh, under **Snapping and measuring**, read **Whole mesh** (width x height x depth, area, volume). Press key **1** (vertices), click two corners:
   **Selection** shows their distance and the x, y, z difference. Select edges: it shows their total length; faces: their area.
5. **Snapping.** Set **Snap to** to **Vertex** (or Edge or Face), tick **Snap (Ctrl)**, select a vertex, press **G** and move the mouse near another vertex: a yellow ring shows
   it and the vertex jumps onto it; the bottom line says "snapping to Vertex". Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
6. **Material library.** Select **Slot House**, Edit Mesh, **Material Slots**: pick a slot, open **Material library** and choose *Copper*: that slot takes the colour. Open **Palette** and choose *Barn*: four slots change at once.
7. **Picture per slot.** In a slot row, type an image path (for example one of your own `Assets/brick.png`) in the **picture path** box: in the software renderer the slot's faces show the picture.
   (The OpenGL and Direct3D renderers still show the colour; that part is not built yet.)
8. **Add to scene as object.** Modeling window > **Import** page > **Add to scene as object**: choose **Exact mesh** and press **Add Copy to Scene**: a copy appears next to the object, with a Mesh Collider (choose **Box** or **No collider** for the others).
9. **Shortcuts and recent tools.** Edit Mesh > **Shortcuts and recent tools** lists the keys and the last tools you used.


**Model faster (same section; real window unverified).** Open `examples\modeling_tools\spin_path_curve.okayscene`: it now also has a **Table** and a **Window Wall** made by the "how do I" recipes.
1. Click **Window Wall**, Modeling window, tick **Edit Mesh** (or press Tab). At the top of the 3D view, under the Object / Edit / Vertex / Edge / Face buttons, you should see a row of small tool buttons (Extrude Faces, Inset Faces, ... Repair Mesh, Sym X, Snap, Repeat, Find...). At the bottom-left a grey line says what to do.
2. Press key **3** (faces), click a face of the wall. Hover **Extrude Faces**: the tooltip says what it does. Click it: the face is pushed out. Press **Shift+R**: it extrudes again. Ctrl+Z twice.
3. **Right-click** (click, do not drag) in the 3D view: a menu of tools that fit the selection appears. Click **Inset Faces**.
4. Press **Ctrl+K**: a box opens. Type `bevel`: *Bevel Edges* is first (greyed out until edges are selected; hover for why). Clear it and type `window`: *Make a Window Hole (how do I)*. Select a wall face, press Ctrl+K, type `window`, press **Enter**: an opening with a frame is cut.
5. Select a few faces and press Ctrl+K, type `similar`, Enter on *Select Similar: Facing*: every face pointing the same way is selected. Try *Grow Selection*, *Shrink Selection*, *Select Up-Facing Faces*.
6. Edge mode (key **2**), click an edge, Ctrl+K, `round`, Enter: the edge is rounded. Ctrl+K, `table`, Enter: a new **Table** object appears (Edit Mesh, Material Slots recolours top and legs).
7. Open Edit Mesh > **Shortcuts and recent tools**: the **Recent** line lists your tools; **Undo history** lists them with names. Click an older step: the mesh goes back to before it.
8. Scale an object (the Inspector scale to 2, 1, 1), then Ctrl+K, `apply scale`, Enter: the scale returns to 1 and the mesh is as wide as before (the Measure line stays the same).

**Hide, drag-select and more (same section; real window unverified).** In `examples\modeling_tools\spin_path_curve.okayscene` the **House Roof Hidden** object has its roof faces hidden.
1. Click **House Roof Hidden**, tick Edit Mesh (Tab). Press **Alt+H**: the red roof faces appear and are selected. Press **H**: they hide again. Select a wall and press **/**: only that wall shows (local view); **/** again shows everything. Ctrl+Z steps back through these.
2. Press **B** and drag a rectangle round some vertices (Vertex mode, key 1): they are selected; try **C** (paint with the circle, wheel = size, Esc ends) and **L** (draw a loop). Without X-ray only the front side is picked; press **Alt+Z** (or the X-ray button) and drag again to select through the mesh.
3. Face mode (key 3), select a face, press **Shift+D**: a copy appears and follows the mouse; Enter keeps it. Press **E** on a face: it is dragged out along its normal; type `0.5` and Enter for an exact distance. Press **I**: move the mouse toward the middle of the face; click to keep the inset.
4. Edge mode (key 2): double-click an edge: its whole loop is selected.
5. Press **Sym Y** (or **Z**) in the toolbar, select a vertex, press **G** and move: the partners across that plane move mirrored. In Edit Mesh tick **Start with symmetry on: X**, leave edit mode and enter it again: Symmetry X is already on.
6. Ctrl+click two or more mesh objects in the Hierarchy, press **Ctrl+K**, type `join` and Enter: they become one object. Type `align` for Align Objects, `separate` on a mesh of several pieces to split it into objects, `cursor` then Enter to add a cube where the mouse pointed.

**Vertex colours, creases, shrinkwrap, reduce, library (same section; real window unverified).** Open `examples\modeling_tools\vertex_paint_creases.okayscene`: a **Gradient Bar** already painted red to blue with vertex colours, a **Creased Cube** (its edges are pink in Edit Mesh) next to a plain cube, both with the Subdivision modifier, and a **Wrap Target** sphere.
1. **Vertex colours.** Click **Gradient Bar**: it shows a smooth red-to-blue gradient. Tick Edit Mesh, Paint section, tick **Paint Brush (drag on mesh)** and **Vertex colours (smooth)**, pick green, drag over the bar: the colour blends in smoothly. Ctrl+Z undoes a stroke. Try **Smooth Colours** and **Clear Vertex Colours**. Switch the renderer in the editor's rendering settings (OpenGL, Direct3D 11, software) and look again.
2. **Creases.** Click **Creased Cube** (it has a Subdivision modifier): it stays boxy; the plain cube beside it rounds into a blob. In Edit Mesh press key **2**, click an edge of the plain cube, set **Crease sharpness** to 2, press **Ctrl+K**, type `crease`, Enter: that edge turns pink and stays sharp after subdivision.
3. **Shrinkwrap.** In the Hierarchy click **Gradient Bar**, Ctrl+click **Wrap Target**, tick Edit Mesh on the bar, select a few vertices (key 1), press Ctrl+K, type `snap`, Enter: those vertices jump onto the sphere. Try `shrinkwrap` for the whole mesh and change **Surface offset**.
4. **Reduce Polygons.** Click the **Wrap Target** sphere (many triangles), Edit Mesh, set **Reduce to %** to 25, Ctrl+K, type `reduce`, Enter: the Console shows the triangle count dropping to about a quarter and the sphere still looks round.
5. **Mesh library.** Use **Save as Mesh Asset** on a model, then Modeling > Import page > **Mesh library**: it appears (press Refresh); **Add** puts a copy in the scene.

**Picture.** a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) is a headless software render of the example scene (not a GPU render, not the editor window).

**What was and was not checked.** The tests `modeling_more` and `modeling_more_scene` ran on Linux (slots through scene save/load, `.okaymesh` files,
the software renderer drawing each slot's colour and picture, Repair Mesh, Spin, Extrude Along Path, Array Along Curve, measuring, snapping, the library, the dissolve/weld/delete fixes). Nobody has clicked these buttons in the real
editor window (the editor code was only syntax-checked, the snapping ring and the buttons in steps 1 to 9 are unseen), run the Windows build, or looked at the OpenGL, Direct3D 11 or Direct3D 12 renderers (they draw per-face colours, as before).

## 7zi. Guided architecture: walls, stairs, doors, windows, roofs, buildings

**What it is.** More things on the Modeling window's **Guided** page, built on the same rules as the fence (7zg): every
model is an ordinary mesh, parts have names, and rebuilding never overwrites your hand edits without asking.

- **Wall** along a straight run or a path with windows and a door cut in and filled with real windows and doors (corners are
  butt-joined, best at right angles). **Stairs**: straight, L, U and spiral with side boards and railings (landing edges have no
  railing). **Door**: flat, panelled, glazed, planks, double; frame, handle, can stand open. **Window**: five bar layouts, three
  frames, sill, shutters. **Roof**: gable, hip, shed, flat, with an overhang and trim. **Building**: walls, windows, a door and a roof
  composed as parts, 1 to 6 floors.

**Status.** Generation and rebuild rules are tested on Linux (`ctest -R guided_architecture`, about 1400 checks:
every design sound and closed, parts never overlap, every setting at its limits, a fuzz, swapping windows, door and roof of a
building, your edits and your own additions surviving). The page itself was never opened in a real window; nothing ran on Windows.
Pictures in a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) and `building_part_swap_before_after.png` are headless renders of the
generated meshes, not editor screenshots.

**Try it.**

1. **File > Examples > Guided modeling (fences, buildings, stairs...) > guided_architecture** (or File > Open... on
   `examples\modeling\guided_architecture.okayscene`). A grid of 29 models, one row per kind: walls, stairs, doors, windows, roofs,
   buildings (the rows are 14 m apart; use the Hierarchy and F to find them).
2. Click a building in the Hierarchy, open Modeling > Guided. Drag **Floors**, **Roof pitch**, **Width**: the building rebuilds.

   Change that window's design: it asks (Keep my edits / Discard my edits / Convert to regular mesh).
4. Click a wall, set **Door** on, **Windows** to 3. Draw your own wall: **Size > Draw in the Scene view**, then click points on the

**What it is.** Characters on the Modeling window's **Guided** page, same rules as 7zg to 7zj, including the **Detail** level (Low to Ultra).

setting at its limits, fuzz, swapping hands, hair, hats, proportions, creature body plans, your edits and your own additions surviving). The page
was never opened in a real window; nothing ran on Windows. Pictures (a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) sheets and

Humans from Medium up are organic (lofted body, separate face parts); robots and creatures are blocky; spiders and insects have crude legs. A human can be given a skeleton and skin weights (see step 8). What is checked: `ctest -R guided_animation`.

**Try it.**

1. **File > Examples > Guided modeling > guided_characters** (26 characters: humans, robots and creatures in rows, 4 m apart). Click one in the
   Hierarchy, open Modeling > Guided.
2. **Proportions**: drag Height, Shoulder width, Head size, Leg length, Limb thickness; **Pose**: Arm angle, Elbow bend, Leg spread.
3. **Parts and materials**: change Hair, Hat, Glasses, Top, Bottoms, Hands, Feet, Backpack, Belt, Cape, Shoulder pads; change a colour.
4. **Each part > Hands**: give one hand its own design (Select jumps to it in Edit Mesh; move it with G, return: "[edited by you]"; change the
   Hands design for all: it asks first). Add your own geometry in Edit Mesh: it stays when you change settings.
5. **Creatures**: pick the Dragon, change **Wing span**, **Tail** and **Horns**; pick a Dog and change **Ears**; **Body plan** switches the layout.
6. **Detail**: Low, Medium, High, Ultra (triangle counts shown). Collision: Exact (mesh) / None.
7. To make your own: Modeling > Guided with nothing selected, Characters, pick a design card, Create. Select faces and **Save selection as part**
   to keep a hat or hand of your own as a design.
8. **Styles and looks** (a human): **Style** under Proportions (realistic, stylised low poly, cartoon, blocky: blocky stays boxes at every Detail
   level, stylised shows its facets, cartoon has a big head and short limbs). New **Hair** (buzz, bob, ponytail, afro, curly, side part, braid),
   **Head** (heart, long, wide), **Top** (tank, long sleeve, hoodie), **Bottoms** (jeans, cargo, leggings, long skirt) and a **Scarf**.
9. **Animation**: with a human selected open **Animation (skeleton)**. **Make animated copy** adds a skinned human with 15 bones next to it.
   To see it move: add a player to the scene (GameObject menu, Third Person Player), select the human and press **Use as the player's
   character**, then Play and walk with W. The engine's own idle and walk play on the bones (the same path an imported humanoid takes).

**What the animation test proves.** `guided_animation` builds the skeleton for every human design at Medium and High (all 15 bones map, every vertex has weights, no bone is dead), puts one on the engine's third-person player, and checks that idle then W moves the body more than a metre, swings the thighs more than 8 degrees apart, deforms the skin and keeps it finite and person-sized. It does not judge how nice the bending looks: weights are by distance to the bones, so shoulders, hips and the crotch bend roughly, and clothes and hair follow the nearest bone.

**Not done / unverified.** No facial expressions or finger joints; clothes are shells around the body, not cloth; the rig button and the page's Detail control were never clicked in a window; the rigged copy is a snapshot (it is not kept in step with later changes); only humans have a skeleton (robots and creatures do not).

## 7zo. Guided: changing settings no longer lags

**What it is.** The Guided page used to freeze for a moment (a second or more on a car or a person at Ultra) when you moved a slider, picked a design or
changed Detail, and it cost a little on every frame just by being open. It is fixed: sliders show a cheap live preview while you drag, the real model is built
once when you let go (one undo step), and a time line under the Undo buttons tells you what the last change cost. Numbers and causes: `docs/guided_perf.md`.

**Status.** The engine side is tested on Linux (`ctest -R guided_perf`, about 1,240 checks, plus the existing guided tests). The panel changes
(`editor/GuidedPanel.cpp`) compile but nobody has opened them in a real window yet (unverified). Nothing here ran on Windows.

**Try it.**

1. Open **File > Examples > Guided modeling > guided_vehicles**, click a car, open **View > Editors & Tools > Modeling** and press **Guided**.
2. Under **Detail** press **Ultra** (about 100,000 triangles). Under the Undo buttons you now see a line like
   `Last change: 300 ms (build 40, mesh 40, save 190) ... 107272 triangles`. That is the real cost of the change.
3. Open **Size** and drag a slider such as **Length**. While you hold the mouse the car follows at Medium detail (the line shows `Drag preview: 1 ms`).
   Let go: the car is rebuilt at Ultra once. **Undo guided step** goes back one step for the whole drag, not one per tick.
4. Leave the panel open and do nothing: the editor should stay smooth (before, a big model cost several milliseconds every frame).
5. Hand edits: in Edit Mesh move one wheel, go back to Guided and drag a slider. There is no preview for a model with hand edits (it cannot keep them); it is
   rebuilt when you let go and keeps your edit. The time line then says it did the full check.
6. Buses, trucks and buildings at Ultra no longer come apart (the windows used to float off the body); the tipper truck bed now sits on the chassis.

**Not done / unverified.** The panel was not run in a window, so the preview feel and the real frame times are unverified. The cape of the Hero human still hangs
a few centimetres off the back (a design choice); `guided_pictures` renders were not re-made.

## 7zq. Modeling: curves, bevel weights, remesh, undo and attribute fixes

**What it is.** More of the modeler (same Modeling window as 7zh): Bezier curves to meshes, edge bevel weights, Quad Remesh, saved reference images, and fixes so edits keep material slots, UVs, vertex colours and seams.

**Steps.** Open the Modeling window and follow these.

More new steps (same branch):
- **Curves and bevel weights example**: File > Open `examples\modeling_tools\curves_bevel.okayscene` (picture: a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository)). You see a pipe, a flat ribbon, a swept square tube and a cube with only its top edges rounded, with three hint lines on screen. Press Play to look at it, Stop to edit. Select the cube, open Edit Mesh: its top edges are drawn green (bevel weights).
- **Coloured edges**: in Edit Mesh, creased edges are pink and bevel-weighted edges are green. Select two edges, Ctrl+K, type "crease" or "bevel weight", run Set; the colours appear at once. Clear removes them.
- **Quad Remesh**: add a Sphere, open Modeling > Edit Mesh, set "Quads target" to 300, press Ctrl+K and run "Quad Remesh". The Console says how many triangles became how many quads, and the sphere is now made of quads (switch on the wireframe to see them). Undo brings the old mesh back. Limits: it does not follow flow lines; slots, vertex colours and UVs are dropped.
- **Reference images are saved**: Import page > Reference images: add a PNG, save the scene, reopen it: the picture plane is still there (path, plane, size, opacity, flip, visible).
- **Direct3D per-slot pictures** (Windows, Direct3D 11 or 12 renderer): give two slots different pictures on the Material slots page; each slot should show its own picture. Written but never run on a GPU.
- **Mirror and Undo fixes** (Edit Mesh): add a Mirror modifier to a half model that has UVs or material slots; the mirrored half now keeps its picture and colours. In Edit Mesh, add a modifier from the Inspector, change the mesh, then press Ctrl+Z: the modifier list goes back together with the mesh (Ctrl+Y brings both back). Edge snapping ignores the hidden diagonal inside a quad.
- **Faces keep their look through edits**: in Edit Mesh on a mesh with two material slots (Material slots page) and UVs, select a face and Extrude, Inset, Subdivide, Poke or Duplicate it, or delete a face; the new faces keep the slot colour of the face they came from and the picture does not jump. The same holds for the Array, Solidify, Subdivision, Decimate and Displace modifiers (add one in the Inspector > Modifiers).
- **Slots: remove and reorder; UVs survive edits** (Edit Mesh > Material slots page): with two or more slots, pick one and press `- Slot` (its faces fall back to slot 0, later slots move down) or `Up` / `Down` (faces keep their colour, the slot just changes place). Ctrl+Z undoes each. UVs: unwrap a mesh (UV page > Smart Unwrap), then Subdivide or Poke a few faces: the new faces keep the UV layout (no jump or stretch in the UV view) and marked seams stay seams, including through the Array and Subdivision modifiers.

**What it is.** The 3D modeler can now give faces to numbered material slots. Each slot has a colour, and changing a slot's colour

**Status.** The engine side is covered by the Linux tests `modeling_more`, `modeling_more_scene` and `modeling_fuzz` (headless). The editor buttons and menus here were not compiled with the editor on Linux and not clicked in the Windows editor; the Direct3D 11/12 and OpenGL per-slot drawing never ran on a GPU. The picture a picture folder (pictures are no longer stored in the repository) is a headless software render.

## 7zr. Damaged prefab variants and deep project folders

What changed: a variant prefab file that was cut off in the middle of its last line (a crash or a full disk while
saving, a bad copy) used to load anyway, quietly missing the half-written record (for example a colour or tag
override). It is now refused with an error that says the file is cut short, and the scene is left as it was.

1. In the editor, make a prefab, then **Create Variant** of it, and change something on the variant (a tag) so the
   variant file has an `override` line.
2. Close the editor. Open the variant `.okayprefab` in Notepad. Delete the end of the file from the middle of an
   `override ...` line onwards (keep `override 2 ` and delete the rest), and save.
3. Start the editor and drag the variant into the scene. You should see an error that names the variant and says
   "cut short", and nothing is added. Before this change the variant appeared without that override.
4. Deep folders: put the project in a folder whose full path is longer than 260 characters and repeat steps 1 and 3
   with an undamaged variant. It should load normally.

Also fixed for deep folders on Windows (code only): a file dragged onto the editor window from a deep folder kept
only the first 520 characters of its path; the editor's own path (used to find the player, plugins, downloads and
crash reports) was cut at 260 characters; the crash report folder was cut at 260 characters.

**Checks run for this change** (Linux): `prefab_variants` passed with 201 different temp folder path lengths
(about 100 to 300 characters); its new suite cuts a variant in a folder over 300 characters deep at every byte, and
failed before the fix (82 cuts in the middle of a line loaded). `ctest -R "prefab|scene|asset|path"`: see the PR.

**Not seen:** the editor steps above were not run; the Windows changes (drag and drop, editor path, crash folder,
`Backend::BasePath`) were only syntax-checked with MinGW, not built or run on Windows.

## 7zsd. Sandbox digging: first and third person

**What it is.** The Sandbox's digger now aims the same way in both views. The aim line always goes through the
crosshair (the centre of the screen). In third person it starts where that line passes the character (not at the lens
behind you), the reach is measured from the character, and it will not dig inside your own body, with your head in the
ground, or the ground behind a wall you are looking over. The same Player Controller View setting (First Person,
Third Person, Both) is used; the Sandbox template now uses Both and starts in first person.

**Steps.**
1. Open the editor, choose New Project > Sandbox (or File > Examples > voxel > `voxel_sandbox`), press Play.
2. Look at the ground. A hollow orange marker shows where you will dig. Hold left mouse (or RT on a pad): the ground
   goes, the marker shrinks and turns white as the ground under it is taken away. Right mouse (or LT) builds.
3. Press V (or Back on a pad) to switch to third person. Dig again: the marker is still under the crosshair, and
   ground more than 14 m from the character is out of reach (the marker disappears).
4. Stand with a wall of ground between you and a spot you look at over your shoulder: it will not dig that spot.
5. Press 1 to 9 to pick the material to build with, or use the mouse wheel or the bumpers (LB / RB) to step through
   them. With a terrain that has no materials, the wheel changes the brush size instead. T (or a click on the right
   stick) picks the material under the crosshair.
6. Rebind: the actions are named Dig, Place, PickBlock, HotbarNext and HotbarPrev (the Input settings / remap
   screen list them; until you rebind Dig and Place they follow Fire and Aim, i.e. left and right mouse, RT and LT). Once an action is rebound its old default button stops working.

**What you should see.** The same dig in both views, a crosshair dot in the middle of the screen, the help line at
the top listing the controls. A material the tool is too weak for (Realistic preset, hardness above the tool
power) shows a red marker.

**Status.** Verified here: the `voxel_aim` test (ray start, reach, wall, body, both views with a real Player
Controller, actions, hotbar, progress, scene save) on Linux. Unverified: nothing was run in a window, on Windows
or with a real pad or touch screen.

## 16. Main menu bar (cleaned up)

What changed and why: [editor_menus.md](editor_menus.md) (the map, and a table of every old item and where it went).
Where: the menu bar at the top of the editor, `Tools\OkayEngine.exe` (or start the editor from the launcher). Open any project.

1. Click **File**. You should see, in this order: New 2D Scene, New 3D Scene, Open Scene... (Ctrl+O), Open Recent, **one** Examples
   (it used to be three), then Save Scene / Save Scene As... / Save Project with their keys, then New Project... / Open Project Folder... /
   Project Upgrade..., then Import Model... / Merge Scene into Current..., then Autosave and Build Settings... (Ctrl+B), then Exit.
   Open **Examples**: UI Gallery, UI Gallery (phone), Visual Script Node Playground, Node Playground (flow and variables).
   With no recent scenes, hover **Open Recent**: the tip says why it is greyed. Press Play, then open File: **Save Scene** is greyed and
   the tip says "Stop Play first ...".
2. Click **Edit**. Undo and Redo name the step ("Undo Move") and are grey, with a tip, when there is nothing to undo. With nothing selected,
   Cut, Copy, Duplicate and Delete are grey ("Select an object ... first."). Select an object: they work. Ctrl+click three objects in the
   Hierarchy, open Edit again: the labels read **Duplicate 3 Objects** and **Delete 3 Objects**, and Cut is grey with the reason. **Preferences**
   holds UI Scale, Density, Theme and Accent color (they used to be View > Appearance). **Project Settings...** is at the bottom.
3. Click **GameObject**. Create Empty, Create Empty Child and Create Empty Parent (Ctrl+Shift+G) come first; Child and Parent need a selection.
   Then the categories: **2D Object, 3D Object, Player, Light, Camera, Audio, Effects, UI**. **Audio > Audio Source** (new) puts a sound object in
   the scene and selects it; its Audio Source component is in the Inspector. Everything the old menu offered is in one of the categories
   (the table in editor_menus.md says which).
4. Click **View**. **Panels**, **Editors & Tools** and **Layout** are where they always were. Below: **Frame Selected (F)**, **Isolate Selection
   (Shift+I)**, **UI Editing Mode**, **Scene Overlays**, **Camera Bookmarks** (hover "Go to slot 1" before saving one: the tip says to save
   first), **Rendering & Performance**. There is no loose "Reset Layout" any more: it is inside **Layout**.
5. Click **Help**. **Documentation (online)** opens the docs folder on GitHub in your browser. **Report a Bug...** opens the issue page and
   puts `OkaySpace v<version>` on the clipboard (paste it somewhere to see). **Check for Updates...** moved here from the old Engine menu.
6. The **Window** and **Engine** menus are gone: their items were duplicates (Items, Loot & Recipes is in View > Editors & Tools; Build
   Settings is in File) or moved (Check for Updates to Help).

## 17. Hierarchy right-click menus

Where: the **Hierarchy** panel (left side by default). Map and the Existing / Gap table: [editor_menus.md](editor_menus.md), section 2.

1. Right-click an object. The menu starts with Copy, Cut, Paste, Paste as Child, then Rename (F2), Duplicate, Delete, Delete Children, then
   Create Empty Child, **Create Child**, Create Parent, Parent To, Unparent, Order, then Select, Expand All Below, then Deactivate, Lock, Focus in
   Scene, Isolate, Transform, then **Add Component...**, Prefab, Save As Prefab..., Rig & IK, Copy Name or Path.

   Sort A-Z. The **[+]** button at the top has Create Empty, Create Empty Child, Group Selected and the same categories.
